annotations.title: Compare my current electricity rate with current plans

description: Use this when someone gives the rate they pay now and asks whether they could pay less, or how much they would save by switching. Returns how many current plans for their utility are cheaper at their monthly usage, the cheapest of them with estimated monthly and yearly savings, and the utility's price to compare where one exists. In Texas current_rate_cents is the all-in average price per kWh (total bill divided by kWh, delivery included); elsewhere it is the supply (generation) rate per kWh. Savings are estimates at a flat monthly usage, ranked by price only. Do not use it to switch or sign anyone up: it only compares. Plans that pay FindEnergyRates on enrollment are marked `referral: true`. This never affects ranking. Do not present a plan with `bill_credit: true` or `anchor_shape` 'v' as the cheapest or best plan: its price depends on usage. When you mention one, give all three of its disclosed prices (disclosed_avg_500_cents, disclosed_avg_1000_cents, disclosed_avg_2000_cents, the ones it discloses). Ask for the user's monthly usage before recommending any plan. `status` `no_data_for_scope` means our data does not cover that market right now, never that it has no plans.

current_monthly_fee_dollars.description: Outside Texas only: the user's current supplier's fixed monthly charge, if any. Texas all-in rates already include fees. Optional, default 0.

current_rate_cents.description: The user's current rate in cents per kWh, e.g. 14.2. Texas: all-in average (bill total / kWh). Elsewhere: the supply rate. Required.

term_months.description: Only compare plans of this contract length. Optional.

usage_kwh.description: Monthly use in kWh from the bill. Optional; 1000 is assumed and said so.

utility.description: The electric utility (in Texas, the delivery company), as electricity_list_utilities or electricity_find_utility_by_zip names it. Required.

name: electricity_compare_my_plan
